description: Solve trig equations across the interval and find every root.

concepts.def: Calculator gives one solution; find others using symmetry.
sin x repeats every 360° (2π); has two solutions per cycle.
cos x repeats every 360°; symmetric about x=0.
tan x has period 180° (π); one solution per cycle.
x = arcsin k and x = 180° - arcsin k, plus multiples of 360°.
Treat 2sin²x - sin x - 1 = 0 as a quadratic in sin x.

mcqs.q: Period of tan x in degrees

options: There are infinitely many roots.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) equals x because the trig functions cancel.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) depends on x and varies between 0 and 2.
1 for all x — the Pythagorean trigonometric identity.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) depends on x and varies between 0 and 2.
No — sin is not a linear function; sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x).
Sin is a function, so sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) by pulling the constant out.
Sin(2x) equals sin(x)^2 by analogy with squaring.
